groups: A first browser GET returns a blank account view without creating a workspace, salt, throttle or session
Anonymous requests and caller-forged authentication headers fail behind the modeled trusted Sites edge
Explicit account-bound creation and reopening create no native credential or pairing code
Browser PDF/profile writes use shared validation and actual private R2; valid native tokens never choose the browser owner
No browser mutation or receipt export accepts a native token or forged caller identity in place of Sites authentication
Every browser mutation rejects stale or missing account/workspace intent before any write, cleanup, throttle, PDF access or provider request
Workspace and bound receipt GETs remain read-only, including changed email and expired dispatch/session rows
All browser writes require the exact Origin and reject cross-site, same-site and navigation Fetch Metadata
The browser allowlist excludes native credential routes, rejects unknown fields, and applies bounded single-pass JSON parsing
Explicit same-account email refresh advances the revision once and invalidates old approval without creating or rotating phone credentials
Stale profile replay and unapproved, changed-digest or old-schema reviews cannot replace data or authorize a send
Explicit approval and continuation submit the exact reviewed PDF/LinkedIn payload once; repeat requests and duplicate reviews do not resend
An ambiguous browser dispatch remains durably uncertain and cannot be automatically retried or duplicated
Stop and provider-unavailable continuation preserve the existing fail-closed submission rules
Manual LinkedIn jobs cause no fetch or receipt; receipt exports remain account-bound and contain no PDF bytes
A deleted and recreated workspace rejects stale requests even when the signed-in account is unchanged
A pending deletion remains visible and read-only while browser creation, mutations and receipt downloads stay locked without cleanup
scope: Bundled production application handler inside actual workerd with real local D1 and R2. Provider HTTP is synthetic and all real outbound requests are forbidden.
limits: The test-only edge strips caller identity headers and injects trusted synthetic owners. Production Sites header stripping, browser UI behavior and production HTTPS require separate live acceptance.
